A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NEO research. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.3 are readable and can be reliably matched.

before.justification: Tables 1–3 and Figures 5–7 report original NEO benchmark results and analyses of architecture, pre-Buffer reuse, and training stages.

after.justification: V2 retains the original benchmark and ablation results and adds an original comparison with EVE variants in Figure 7.

M1.justification: The patch/word embeddings, expanded QK dimensions, Native-RoPE, mixed attention, pre-Buffer/post-LLM architecture, and three-stage training remain unchanged. Expanded initialization documentation does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Training datasets, bilingual coverage, evaluation tasks, and benchmarks are retained, including the instruction datasets in Appendix Table 4. The new EVE comparison uses existing benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: New Figure 7 compares NEO with EVEv1.0, EVEv1.5, and EVEv2.0 using Qwen3-1.7B. These are additional comparator configurations in a dedicated experiment, although some EVE variants already appeared with other backbones in Tables 1–2.

E3.justification: The added architecture comparison fixes the backbone to Qwen3-1.7B within Section 4.3's ablation framework. Table 1 also revises the stated Qwen2.5-VL backbone from Qwen2.5-1.5B to Qwen2.5-3B; its unchanged scores do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 adds an analysis testing whether NEO's advantage persists against dense, MoE, and divide-and-conquer EVE architectures with a common backbone. Existing attention/RoPE, pre-Buffer depth, reuse, and training-stage analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or experimental error bars. Benchmark averaging remains the reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Figure 7 and its discussion report average accuracies of 33.4%, 40.2%, and 41.5% for EVEv1.0, EVEv1.5, and EVEv2.0, respectively, against NEO's 44.0%. Numerical benchmark scores in Tables 1–3 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The embedding and Native-RoPE equations are unchanged. New Equation 3 expresses the pre-normalized attention/FFN residual block already depicted in v1 Figure 3; it adds notation without a substantive mathematical revision, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the performance claim from rivaling top-tier modular models to greatly narrowing their gap; the introduction similarly changes 'rivals' to 'approaches.' The native-primitive and reusable-component contributions are retained.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the common-backbone EVE comparison as evidence that architectural choices explain the gains and refines the discussion of training-data limitations. Appendix A.3 removes the explicit limitation concerning inability to train entirely from scratch and potential language-modality bias.

D1.justification: Section 3.1 expands initialization documentation, including explicit H/W QK-Norm initialization with beta=0 and gamma=1. Section 4.3 specifies projector/new-QK training and subsequent backbone unfreezing for the existing pre-Buffer comparison. Appendix Table 5 and the code/weights release commitment remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Seed1.5-VL, GLM-4.1V, and NaViL references and removes the Claude 3, Gemini 2.5 technical-report, and GPT-4V preliminary-exploration references. It revises modular-model examples and adds PaliGemma attribution when describing mixed attention.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites refine the abstract, primitive explanation, initialization discussion, and experimental interpretations. Citation formatting, affiliations, and author footnotes also change, while the overall section organization and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3 receive revised explanatory panels. Figure 6 consolidates the pre-Buffer bars and omits the full-NEO bar while retaining its comparison in text; new Figure 7 shifts the existing training-stage plot to Figure 8. Tables 1–2 reorder and gray the Qwen2.5-VL row and revise highlighting.

improvement.justification: The common-backbone EVE comparison strengthens empirical support, expanded initialization/retraining details aid reproducibility, and the moderated headline claim better reflects Tables 1–2. Removing Appendix A.3's pretrained-LLM and language-bias caveat reduces transparency, although LLM initialization remains explicit. Overall, the revision provides a limited net improvement.
